title: Choose the event board's visual world
question: The board must work on phones during a live club event and read clearly on a projector. Keep the field-book direction, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Caderno de loteamento
options.lineage: Brazilian survey field books, cadastral maps, and site stakes
options.thesis: Every squad occupies a measured lot, and every human decision leaves a dated field mark.
options.viewport: A projector-scale cadastral sheet fills the screen; live district tiles sit inside measured parcels, while the current round and squad status live in the map margin.
options.risk: The map grammar must stay operational on a narrow phone instead of becoming decorative paperwork.

raised.raise: Color stays concentrated at live state boundaries, so the city remains legible at distance.
Recorded words visibly change the plan only after a decision is dispatched.
Returns and revisions remain as marks in the lot history instead of disappearing.
System state writes itself into the field log instead of hiding behind generic chrome.

options.label: Mural de mutirão
options.lineage: community planning walls, masking tape, index cards, and public assembly notes
options.thesis: The room sees a shared wall where squads pin proposals, cross out cuts, and move accepted work into the city.
options.viewport: The city occupies the center of a wall-sized board, with squad strips and the live round arranged around it like an active workshop.
options.risk: This is the most familiar collaboration metaphor and can slip into generic kanban if the city stops leading.

options.label: Departure rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket airline timetables on a lit slide rack
options.thesis: Rounds become departures, squads become gates, and each dispatch occupies one exact status cell.
options.viewport: A lateral rack shows every squad and round at once, with the city visible as the destination beyond the active slide.
options.case: Its fixed cells make phase and dispatch state exceptionally clear, but the audience identifies less strongly with airline operations than collective building.
options.risk: Dense codes can overwhelm first-time participants on phones.

options.label: One-bit city desk
options.lineage: early one-bit desktops with tiled windows and marching selections
options.thesis: Every squad owns a crisp city window, and accepted artifacts snap into the shared desktop.
options.viewport: The projector is one desktop of tiled district windows; the active steerer and pending decisions invert in place.
options.case: Tool users recognize the grammar immediately, but it makes the city feel like software before it feels like a collective place.
options.risk: Strict monochrome can flatten differences between harnesses and models.

options.label: Flash-scrawl club sleeve
options.lineage: direct-flash club photographs marked up by hand
options.thesis: The event accumulates as one defaced group photograph whose marks record each round.
options.viewport: A live room photograph sits behind the city while every action adds a persistent hand mark.
options.case: It captures the club's energy, but it obscures operational state and requires photography the event setup does not guarantee.
options.kept: Human revisions remain visibly present instead of being replaced by the latest clean state.
options.risk: The projector can become visually noisy before the first round finishes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished responsive dashboard with cards, tabs, a city panel, and familiar admin forms.
canonCard.viewport: A top navigation bar, status cards, and the city in a large central panel.
canonCard.risk: Clear and familiar, but indistinguishable from a generic event dashboard.
